data.body:
[operator-attested] EVIDENCE FOR AC4 AND AC5

Both criteria rest on artifacts that do not live in the repository tree — executed command
output, CI votes, and the audit reasoning for sites deliberately NOT changed (a non-change
leaves no diff to discover). Recording them here per the verifier's stated evidence path.

=== AC4 [operator-attested] — audit of every other dir-then-first-file site ===

Method: enumerated every `mkdir` / `makedirs` reachable from the store write path across
src/rebar, then classified each by whether an interruption between the mkdir and the first
file write could leave a path the ticket scanners report.

CONVERTED (all in commit 61b49deaa6, verifiable by diff):
1. `_store/event_append.py::batch_stage_and_commit` — shares `_prepare_event` with the
   single-event path, so it carried the identical window; both now publish through
   `StagedEvent.promote()`. Its docstring had already conceded "a crash mid-batch leaves at
   most orphaned worktree files". `_rollback_batch` additionally removes a directory the
   batch itself published once its event is gone. Covered by
   `test_interrupted_batch_create_leaves_no_debris`.
2. `_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py::_write_event_file` — mkdir preceded
   `_seam.finalize_event`, which can refuse an event outright (the write-time secret screen
   raises CommandError), and preceded lock acquisition, which can time out. Staging now
   happens after finalize.
3. `_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_one.py` BRIDGE_ALERT emission — mkdir then first alert
   file, on an error path (where interruption is most likely).

EXEMPT, with reasons (each verified against the current tree):
4. `_store/lock.py::_acquire_mkdir` — creates `.ticket-write.lock.d`, dot-prefixed and thus
   invisible to `_ticket_dirs` / `foreign_store_path_list`; its own mkdir->stamp-write gap is
   already handled by the staleness adjudicator (`lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale`), so
   converting it would duplicate an existing, more specific mechanism.
5. `_store/hlc.py::_hlc_lock` — creates `.rebar/`, which is outside the tracker worktree
   entirely; an empty `.rebar/` is normal and unscanned.
6. `_commands/fsck_repair.py::_repair_run` — marker dir under the RESOLVED GIT DIR, never the
   committed tree (its own comment says so, so `git add` cannot pick it up).
7. `_commands/session_log.py::_write_pointer`, `_commands/identity.py::_write_pointer`,
   `_commands/trusted_env_cmd.py::_dump` — pointer/config writers that do not write into the
   tracker at all, so no scanner can see their directories.
8. `_commands/init.py` — the init mkdir lock, dot-prefixed and pre-store.

The classification rule is uniform: a site is in scope only if an interruption can leave a
NON-dot-prefixed directory under the tracker root, which is exactly what `fsck._ticket_dirs`
and `fsck.foreign_store_path_list` enumerate. Sites 4-8 fail that test by construction.

=== AC5 [operator-attested] — gates and suites ===

Run in the worktree venv on the merged tree (HEAD 61b49deaa6):
  `make lint`      -> "No findings to report. Good job!" (ruff check + format-check, zizmor,
                      actionlint) — exit 0
  `make typecheck` -> "Success: no issues found in 516 source files" (mypy) — exit 0
  `pytest tests/unit/test_store.py tests/unit/test_store_batch_write.py
          tests/interfaces/store tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py
          tests/unit/test_store_write_index_reset_on_failure.py
          tests/unit/test_store_delete_events.py`
                   -> 466 passed, 9 skipped
  `pytest -k "reconciler or bridge or dispatch or inbound or translate or module_size or
              concurrency"`
                   -> 3067 passed, 24 skipped (after fixing 4 regressions my first cut of the
                      AC4 conversions introduced: the reconciler paths reached the old
                      `mkdir(parents=True)` with the tracker root absent, so `stage_event`
                      now creates it — the tracker root is not the debris signature)
  `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_atomic_ticket_dir_create_021d.py` -> 9 passed
  post-merge re-verification -> 35 passed, `make lint` clean

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: Gerrit change 1696 carried `Verified +1` (GitHub Actions runs
build/test/lint/typecheck on the exact patchset) AND `LLM-Review +1`, and was submitted only
after both. Merged as 61b49deaa6.

NO EVENT-FORMAT OR LAYOUT CHANGE: the committed bytes still come from the single canonical
serializer (`canonical_bytes` / `canonical_str`) — the staging helper receives already-
serialized bytes and only changes WHERE they are written before the rename, never WHAT.
The I2 filename contract (`{timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json`) is unchanged, and the published
ticket directory contains exactly its event files (the ownership stamp is removed before the
rename precisely so it is never published), pinned by
`test_successful_create_publishes_dir_and_event_together`.
